cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where user-supplied data is used to construct database connection URLs, load classes, or configure resources without adequate validation, allowing attackers to inject dangerous parameters, load arbitrary classes, or trigger deserialization and SSRF. The fixes involve adding blacklists, encoding, type checks, or prefix validation.
guideline_text: Trace externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers into privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access. Report code paths where caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect.

mechanism.missing_guard: caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins
mechanism.name: missing authentication before privileged action
mechanism.sink_shape: privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access
mechanism.source_shape: externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers
mechanism.typical_fix: require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Improve regex to match all parameter patterns, iteratively decode URL, or use safe glob-to-regex conversion.
sub_patterns.name: Bypass of JDBC parameter validation via insufficient decoding or regex
sub_patterns.root_cause: Existing validation (blacklist) can be bypassed by URL-encoding, double-encoding, or inadequate regex that fails to capture all parameter syntax variants.
